label: Merchant Profile
title: Merchant Profile
summary: Use a Merchant Profile at the top of a payment to show who is being paid: the merchant’s logo, registered name, and UPI ID.
corePrinciple: Who you’re paying, before how much.

states.title: Wrapped, never cut
states.description: The profile has no states: it doesn’t press. In a narrow column both lines wrap and stay centred, and neither ends in an ellipsis, though Figma cuts a long UPI ID. Both examples sit in a 240 px column.
blocks: The name wraps onto three lines.
specimen: HDFC Bank Limited Corporate Banking Services India

examples.title: Long name
examples.description: The name wraps onto three lines.

sizing.title: Centred in its column
sizing.description: The profile has no width of its own: it fills its column, keeps 16 px clear at each side, and centres its lines; Figma draws it 360 px wide. With a one-line name it’s 102 px tall: a 42 px avatar, 12 px, a 20 px name, 12 px, and a 16 px UPI ID. Figma’s name lines are 18 px.

content.title: The registered name, then the UPI ID
content.description: Write title as the merchant’s registered name, the one their bank holds, so people know who they’re paying. Start subtitle with UPI ID: and give the ID they’re paying, so they can check it.
blocks: “UPI ID:” before the ID people pay.

inContext.description: A payment screen opens with the merchant, so people know who they’re paying before they enter the amount. The screen lays out the rest and sends the payment.

sources.title: Use the public Merchant Profile contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Merchant Profile is one component, 360 × 118, with Title and Subtitle text properties and a nested Avatar showing the merchant’s logo. The package takes title, subtitle, and avatarProps: a left-out line shows sample text, and the Avatar shows a stock photo until you pass a logo or initials. The name’s lines are 20 px, not 18, and a long UPI ID wraps where Figma cuts it. accessibilityLabel does nothing, and the whole profile is a heading (reported).
